LESSON: when two populations show a suspicious count relationship, a cheap decisive test is spatial/identity colocation (same rounded lat/lng) plus an asymmetric bidirectional check (does A imply B, does B imply A) — the asymmetry itself (100% vs 89.6% here) is often more informative than either rate alone.
